data.title: Route Overview
paragraphs: The first rule of this journey is that altitude sets the pace. Two quiet days in Leh come before major drives, giving the body time to adapt while introducing Ladakhi architecture, markets, and the layered Buddhist culture of the Indus valley.

From there, Tsering links monasteries and villages west of Leh with the stark high-desert landscapes toward Hanle. Dark-sky observation is treated as an environmental experience rather than a guaranteed astronomy show, always dependent on weather and local conditions.
highlights: Two-day acclimatisation window before longer high-altitude drives.
Indus valley monastery visits including Thiksey or Hemis according to timing.
Alchi and Lamayuru landscapes interpreted through art, geology, and village life.
Dark-sky nights around Hanle with strict respect for local rules and observatory sensitivity.

introParagraphs: This 9-day journey is paced around monastic culture & dark skies, realistic transfers, and enough time in each region for the place to develop beyond first impressions.
data.title: Detailed Progression

paragraphs: Arrive in Leh and deliberately keep the first day quiet. Gentle neighbourhood walks, hydration, and rest come before any ambitious sightseeing, with a second day used for low-intensity cultural orientation.
listItems: Short old-town walk only after adequate rest.
Flexible visits based on individual acclimatisation.

paragraphs: Travel west for Alchi’s artistic heritage, village lanes, and the dramatic geology around Lamayuru, staying overnight so the long road is not compressed into a day trip.

data.title: HIGH-ALTITUDE SAFETY NOTE
data.text: This itinerary should never override medical advice or individual acclimatisation. Headache, nausea, unusual fatigue, or sleep disturbance must be taken seriously, and route changes should remain possible without treating them as failure.

data.title: A Journey Designed Around Restraint
paragraphs: Ladakh rewards travellers who stop measuring the day by distance. A monastery courtyard, an old irrigation channel, or a night sky can hold more meaning than another pass added for bragging rights.
The route is deliberately spacious because altitude, weather, and community rhythm are part of the landscape, not inconveniences to overcome.

items.question: Can Monasteries Under the Milky Way be tailored to our dates and interests?
paragraphs: Yes. Tsering Namgyal’s route is a design framework rather than a fixed group departure. Stays, activity intensity, and specialist visits can be adjusted while protecting the geographic logic of the journey.
items.listTitle: Common ways to personalise the route:
listItems: Add or remove a night at the most important base.
Reduce walking or replace it with a lower-intensity alternative.
Add a specialist food, craft, wildlife, or photography focus where locally appropriate.

items.question: What is the best season for this journey?
paragraphs: This itinerary should never override medical advice or individual acclimatisation. Headache, nausea, unusual fatigue, or sleep disturbance must be taken seriously, and route changes should remain possible without treating them as failure.

items.question: What is included in the estimated journey budget?
listItems: Handpicked accommodation described in the final confirmed proposal.
Private or pre-arranged ground transfers listed in the route.
Specialist guiding and scheduled cultural or nature experiences.
On-ground coordination for the confirmed itinerary.

items.question: How physically demanding is the itinerary?
paragraphs: The default pace is described as acclimatised. Walking, altitude, wildlife activity, or outdoor intensity varies by region, so the final version should be adjusted to the traveller’s fitness, health, and comfort.
listItems: Alternative or shorter activity options are used where practical.
Weather and local conditions can change the day plan.

items.question: How far in advance should we plan?
paragraphs: For small lodges, specialist guides, rail or ferry seats, light-aircraft sectors, or permit-sensitive experiences, planning several months ahead gives the best flexibility. The exact lead time depends on season and destination.

items.question: How are reservations confirmed and scheduled?
paragraphs: Once the final route, accommodation, and specialist experiences are approved, a 30% confirmation deposit is used to secure services. The remaining balance is normally due 45 days before arrival unless a supplier requires different terms.

items.question: What is the policy for date changes or cancellations?
paragraphs: We try to shift dates or restructure the route whenever suppliers allow, but remote lodges, permits, flights, ferries, and specialist appointments may carry their own non-refundable conditions.
listItems: 60+ days before arrival: refund or credit is calculated after non-refundable supplier costs.
30–59 days before arrival: partial refund or rescheduling credit depends on confirmed supplier terms.
Less than 30 days before arrival: cancellation follows the individual confirmed service conditions.
